# ESXi host loses access to storage device (All Paths Down) — vob.storage.apd.start

## Issue/Introduction
The ESXi host reports that a storage device entered the All Paths Down (APD) state.

## Symptoms
- `/var/run/log/vobd.log` shows `[vob.storage.apd.start] Device or filesystem with identifier [naa.600a0980...] has entered the All Paths Down state.`
- Virtual machines on the affected datastore become unresponsive.
- vCenter Server raises the alarm "Lost access to volume".

## Environment
VMware vSphere ESXi 8.0
VMware vSphere ESXi 7.0

## Cause
All paths to the LUN are unavailable because of a storage array port failure, a zoning change, or an FC/iSCSI fabric outage.
The host keeps retrying I/O until the APD timeout (default 140 seconds) expires.

## Resolution
1. Identify the affected device and the state of each path:
   ```
   esxcli storage core path list -d naa.600a0980XXXXXXXX
   esxcli storage core device list -d naa.600a0980XXXXXXXX
   ```
2. Check the array and fabric (switch port, zoning) with the storage team and restore at least one path.
3. After the paths recover, rescan the adapters:
   ```
   esxcli storage core adapter rescan --all
   ```
4. Confirm `[vob.storage.apd.exit]` appears in vobd.log.

## Workaround
If the device will not come back, unmount the datastore and detach the device to stop retries, then migrate the VMs with vSphere HA or manually.

## Additional Information
See also KB 900002 for Permanent Device Loss (PDL).
